text:
Seth Jarvis missed the start of the season after shoulder surgery and has played 11 games since returning. He has 9 points, 7 of them assists, and Carolina has won most of the games he's played, taking 58.5% of the expected goals at five on five (the quality of chances) with him on the ice.

This isn't yet the player who scored 32 goals last season. He has 2 goals on 2.7 expected, no power-play points, and his ice time has dipped to 16.3 minutes over his last ten. None of that is luck in either direction; his finishing is close to his chances. It reads like a player getting his timing back on a deep team.

The underlying game is intact. Evolving-Hockey had him 42nd among 401 forwards in wins above replacement last season, with almost three goals of value just from drawing penalties. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the slot often and carrying the puck in on 54% of his entries. Watch the power play: when he gets back on it, the points should climb.
headline: Jarvis is back, and Carolina is winning with him
